LESSON: WRITING 8.3.1 CREATIVE WRITING – SHORT STORY

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.3: Writing 8.3.1 Creative writing – short story
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 8.3.1 Creative writing – short story, part of Strand 8 in Grade 9 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: How can we differentiate a short story from a novel? 2. Why is it important for a community to honour its heroes and heroines?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. read a short story from print or digital sources on community legends,

2. work jointly with peers to examine the features of a short story,

3. make notes on the features of a short story,

4. identify a community or national hero and heroine and their unique qualities,

5. prepare an outline of a short story featuring the community or national hero or heroine,

6. use the outline to write a short story on the hero or heroine,

7. share their story with peers for review,

8. publish their refined short story in a school or public magazine. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read a short story from print or digital sources on community legends,
2. work jointly with peers to examine the features of a short story,
3. make notes on the features of a short story,
4. identify a community or national hero and heroine and their unique qualities,
5. prepare an outline of a short story featuring the community or national hero or heroine,
6. use the outline to write a short story on the hero or heroine,
7. share their story with peers for review,
8. publish their refined short story in a school or public magazine. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 8.3.1 Creative writing – short story together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital Literacy: This is promoted as the learner interacts with digital content when reading a short story from digital

sources on community legends.

• Self-efficacy: It is promoted as the learner shows concerted attention by using the outline to write a short story on the hero

or heroine.

Values:
• Patriotism: The learner identifies a community or national hero and heroine and their unique qualities.

• Respect: The learner appreciates diverse opinions when sharing their story with peers for review.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social cohesion is promoted as the learner works with peers to write, peer review and revise the short stories featuring a

community legendary hero or heroine.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept of writing short stories to their learning of the concept of creative writing in English.
